Djamaa el Kebir.fact: The mosque was severely damaged during the French bombardment of Algiers in 1682 and again in 1683, resulting in the subsequent reconstruction of its mihrab and its qibla (southern) wall. The gallery at the outside of the mosque was built in 1837 during French colonial rule.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: Earlier, the mosque was located on the Rue de la Marine in Algiers during French colonial rule of _____, which was then the entrance street to Algiers Harbor
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: Earlier, the mosque was located on the Rue de la Marine in Algiers during French colonial rule of Algeria, which was then the entrance street to Algiers Harbor.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: The central aisle is wider than the others, hinting at the T-plan layout which would become standard in subsequent mosque architecture in _____
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: The central aisle is wider than the others, hinting at the T-plan layout which would become standard in subsequent mosque architecture in Maghreb.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: The mihrab, which was originally built as an integral part of the mosque in _____, was destroyed by the 17th-century French bombardment
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: The mihrab, which was originally built as an integral part of the mosque in 1097, was destroyed by the 17th-century French bombardment.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: The reconstructed mihrab is a typical design followed in 18th-century _____ in the form of indented lobed arches at the end of the central and a much wider nave
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: The reconstructed mihrab is a typical design followed in 18th-century Algiers in the form of indented lobed arches at the end of the central and a much wider nave.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: While the rails that were used to shift the minbar are still embedded in the floor, the minbar itself is now preserved in the _____ of Antiquities and Islamic Arts in Algiers
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: While the rails that were used to shift the minbar are still embedded in the floor, the minbar itself is now preserved in the National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts in Algiers.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: As a result, a gallery or portico of columns was added at the entrance to the mosque and was built in _____ under French colonial rule in an orientalizing style of polylobed arches
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: As a result, a gallery or portico of columns was added at the entrance to the mosque and was built in 1837 under French colonial rule in an orientalizing style of polylobed arches.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: It reuses _____ marble columns from the 18th-century al-Sa'ida Mosque

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: It is one of the finest sculpted minbars of its type in _____
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: It is one of the finest sculpted minbars of its type in Algeria.

Djamaa el Kebir.fact: It bears an inscription in Kufic Arabic script saying: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أتم هذا المنبر في أول شهر رجب من سنة تسعين وأربعمائة.

Djamaa el Kebir.subject: Women & Society
Djamaa el Kebir.question: الذي عمل محمد In the name of Allah, the _____, the Merciful
Djamaa el Kebir.fact: الذي عمل محمد In the name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: The _____ was Culinary tradition of Djibouti.
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Djiboutian cuisine is a mixture of Somali, Afar, Yemeni, and French cuisine, with some additional South Asian (especially Indian) culinary influences.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: Local dishes are commonly prepared using a variety of _____ spices, ranging from saffron to cinnamon
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Local dishes are commonly prepared using a variety of Middle Eastern spices, ranging from saffron to cinnamon.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: It is similar to the _____ injera, but smaller and thinner
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: It is similar to the Ethiopian injera, but smaller and thinner.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: Pasta (baasto) is frequently presented with a heavier stew than the _____ pasta sauce, but is otherwise served in a similar manner as the rice
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Pasta (baasto) is frequently presented with a heavier stew than the Italian pasta sauce, but is otherwise served in a similar manner as the rice.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: Spicy dishes come in many variations, from the traditional fah-fah or soupe _____ (spicy boiled beef soup), to the yetakelt wet (spicy mixed vegetable stew)
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Spicy dishes come in many variations, from the traditional fah-fah or soupe djiboutienne (spicy boiled beef soup), to the yetakelt wet (spicy mixed vegetable stew).

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: Garoobey is one of the staple dishes of _____
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Garoobey is one of the staple dishes of Djibouti. They are part of the four essential elements of the Djiboutian afternoon tea.

Djiboutian cuisine.subject: Women & Society
Djiboutian cuisine.question: Bajiyos, the _____ version of the Indian pakora, are a regular fixture at the table and in street shops, particularly when it is time to break the fast during Ramadan
Djiboutian cuisine.fact: Bajiyos, the Somali version of the Indian pakora, are a regular fixture at the table and in street shops, particularly when it is time to break the fast during Ramadan.
